Interactive space archaeology

Humanity left things behind. Go find them.

Spacecraft finish their missions, but they never leave. Explore the Moon and Mars through two interactive experiences, then read the stories of the machines still resting there.

Choose an experience How it works

Two ways to explore

Start with the guided story, or jump straight into the 3D game. Both open full screen and you can come back here at any time.

Guided story

Forgotten Explorers

Click glowing relics on the Moon and Mars and follow each mission’s story step by step, from launch to its final signal.

  • Moon and Mars
  • Animated timelines
  • Mouse or touch
3D exploration game

Relics of the Cosmos

Pick a planet, land on the surface and look around with your own sensors. Walk up to mission debris and inspect it to read its file.

  • Moon or Mars
  • First-person view
  • Keyboard and mouse

How it works

No sign-up, nothing to install. It runs right in your browser.

Pick an experience

Choose the guided story or the 3D game above. Each one opens full screen.

Find the glowing objects

Relics are highlighted on the surface. Click or tap them, or walk up and press E in the game.

Read their stories

Every relic has a date, a status and the goals it achieved. Press Home to return here.

Good to know: best on a desktop or laptop in Google Chrome. The game uses your keyboard and mouse, and press Esc to release the mouse before clicking Home. An internet connection is required.

Abandoned, but not forgotten.

Every mission ends. When the last signal fades, the hardware stays where it landed: a lander on a dusty plain, a rover in its final position, a lunar module standing on the Moon.

This project gives those machines their stories back, so the next person to look up knows what is out there and why it mattered.
